bull.b: A record customer satisfaction score and repeated independent network awards support durable differentiation in a competitive wireless market. Stronger perceived network quality can improve customer acquisition, retention, and share gains, reinforcing the value of T-Mobile’s nationwide infrastructure.

Strong postpaid service growth and recurring monthly billing provide visible revenue expansion over the next several quarters. Continued account additions, ARPA growth, and service revenue momentum indicate that T-Mobile is monetizing customer demand while expanding its core subscription base.

Improving EBITDA and substantial free cash flow demonstrate that T-Mobile’s operating growth is translating into financial resources. This supports network investment, spectrum participation, debt servicing, and shareholder returns while giving management flexibility to fund multiple strategic priorities.

bear.b: Elevated leverage reduces financial flexibility and leaves more operating cash committed to debt-related obligations. With equity trending lower while debt remains high, T-Mobile may have less capacity to absorb a downturn or simultaneously fund network investment, spectrum, and capital returns.

Planned rate-plan changes may disrupt customer relationships in the near term, while declining prepaid subscribers and revenue indicate pressure in another customer segment. These dynamics could slow net additions and raise the effort or cost required to sustain durable subscriber growth.

Higher device prices combined with unchanged subsidies increase customers’ out-of-pocket burden, especially for price-sensitive users. That can weaken upgrade demand, complicate premium-plan acquisition, and create friction in subscriber growth even if the underlying network proposition remains strong.
